Subject: Dedicated pool questions — throughput guarantees + queueing

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we move into procurement, our infra team has two follow-ups before legal will sign:

1) Can you confirm the per-GPU sustained throughput guarantees you can commit to for our reserved pool (we're planning 8 x A100-equivalent reserved GPUs)? Specifically we want 95th and 99th percentile tokens/sec for both short chat-style requests (<= 256 tokens) and longer batch inference (1k+ tokens).

2) How does Redwood handle queueing when our reserved capacity is saturated? We need to understand preemption, tenant fairshare, and any hard limits that would cause requests to be queued or dropped.

If possible could you share a short, redlined carveout we can take to procurement/infra that outlines any exceptions to the standard SLA (headroom, burst behavior, maintenance windows, and crediting)?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — legal is waiting on the carveout language.

Best,
Alex

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. We're aligned to move fast on this. Quick answers up front, and I'll attach a draft carveout for procurement.

- Throughput: For an 8-GPU reserved pool on our Dedicated SKU we typically guarantee per-GPU baseline throughput equivalent to ~1200 tokens/sec at p95 for short (<=256) sequences and ~850 tokens/sec at p95 for long sequences; p99 figures are ~20-25% higher tail latency depending on model and quantization. Those numbers assume our standard batching and KV-cache behavior; I'll add model-specific breakdowns in the draft.

- Queueing/preemption: Reserved capacity is first-class — your requests get dedicated slots. If tenant usage exceeds the reserved pool, requests are routed to a short overflow queue (max queue depth configurable). Overflow behavior depends on policy: (a) committed-only — reject/limit bursts beyond reservation, (b) best-effort burst — accept into burst capacity (subject to delay), (c) graceful degrade — route to smaller-quantized model variant. We can enumerate the exact policy in the SLA carveout.

I'm attaching a draft PDF that explicitly lists: headroom allowances, burst windows, maintenance window commitments, and the crediting formula if we miss p95/p99 targets. Can we hop on a 30-min call tomorrow with your infra lead so Ben (sales engineer) can walk through the queueing diagram?

Attached: summitai-dedicated-sla-draft.pdf, queueing-flow-diagram.png

Cheers,
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai

Irene / Lauren — forwarding Alex's asks and Irene's draft. A couple of internal notes before we send a formal redline:

1) The throughput numbers Irene quoted are for our baseline LlamaX-13B quant-8 profile. If SummitAI wants a GShard-style 70B family model pinned, the per-GPU throughput changes significantly — we should include a model bucket table rather than hard single numbers.

2) Queue depth: default max overflow queue is 250 concurrent inflight requests per pool; we can propose raising that to 500 for SummitAI during business hours for an additional committed headroom fee. That avoids preemption but needs billing alignment in the contract.

3) Maintenance windows: our standard is one 45-min maintenance monthly with 48h notice; SummitAI asked for a narrower window. Recommend offering a quarterly maintenance waiver for a 30% premium on reserved nodes or alternatively a 2-hr monthly window with guaranteed notification and option to postpone once per quarter.

4) Crediting formula: propose a token-based credit per missed-minute of p95 throughput using the same calculation we use for hosted credits but multiplied by a reserved multiplier (x1.5). Legal will push back on automatic credits; we should offer credits as default with escalation path.

I can jump on the call to discuss queueing-flow and the fee tradeoffs. Thoughts on raising the overflow queue and the premium for maintenance avoidance?

-Ben

Subject: SummitAI — proposed dedicated carveouts and next steps

Alex / Ops team — attaching the redline and diagram we discussed. Summary of the proposed carveouts (high level):

1) Throughput guarantees: We propose model-bucketed guarantees. For your initial LlamaX-13B baseline we will commit to p95 per-GPU sustained throughput of 1,200 tokens/sec (short seq) and 850 tokens/sec (long seq). p99 will be listed as a tail range with a 15-30% tolerance depending on model family and quantization.

2) Overflow/queueing behavior: Default policy is "best-effort burst" with a configurable overflow queue. For SummitAI we propose: max overflow queue depth = 500 during 07:00-19:00 PT (business hours) and 250 off-hours. If the overflow queue depth is exceeded, oldest-in-flight requests will be rate-limited; we will not drop requests without prior consent.

3) Headroom & burst fee: To guarantee the larger overflow queue we require a 20% headroom reservation fee on top of the 8-node commit. This fee buys reserved burst capacity and priority within the cluster.

4) Maintenance windows & notification: We can reduce scheduled monthly maintenance to 30 minutes with 72-hour notice in exchange for a quarterly waiver option sold separately.

5) Crediting & remediation: If p95 commitments are missed for >3 independent days in a 30-day window we provide pro-rated token credits (formula in attached PDF). For severe outages (defined in the doc) we offer a one-time service credit plus expedited remediation steps.

Next steps:
- Ben to confirm overflow queue billing option and put numbers in the redline (end of day tomorrow).
- SummitAI to confirm whether they want the larger overflow depth + headroom fee or prefer a smaller queue and higher credits.
- Legal to review the PDF and push back on automatic crediting language.
